14	- **Reads**: `LINEAR_API_KEY` is in `.env.local` (gitignored). `set -a; source .env.local; set +a` then POST GraphQL to `https://api.linear.app/graphql` with header `Authorization: $LINEAR_API_KEY`. Good for wave/label scans.
15	
16	**The GitHub integration already does the PR bookkeeping.** Opening a PR whose title/branch names the issue (e.g. `MM-472`) auto-attaches it to the issue AND auto-moves the state — observed 2026-07-25: MM-472 went `Done` → back to `In Review` on its own the moment a second PR (#439) opened against it. So after `gh pr create`, **check the issue state before setting it** — a redundant `save_issue(state:…)` is usually unnecessary, and blindly forcing a state can undo what the integration correctly did.
17	
18	**Gotchas:**
19	- The `linear_wave_status` / `linear_list_issues` / `linear_update_issue` tools named in AGENTS.md are **Pi** extension tools (`.pi/extensions/linear/index.ts`), NOT available to Claude Code. Don't try to call them — replicate their GraphQL instead, or use the MCP.
20	- **Writes via Bash** (curl/python hitting the Linear API) are **hard-blocked** by the auto-mode classifier as external-system writes, even with user authorization. Writes must go through the authenticated MCP.
21	- zsh mangles `!` inside heredoc'd GraphQL (`String!` → `String\!`); inline values or put the query in a file written via the Write tool.
22	- The exhaustive `issues(first: 250)` wave-status scan can return HTTP 500; page smaller or filter by label (e.g. `labels: { name: { eq: "Wave 4: Repo + Blobs" } }`).
23	- **Wave labels are team-scoped to MM, not workspace-level.** `list_issue_labels` with NO `team` arg returns an incomplete set (only a few labels) — call it with `team:"MM"` to see the full wave list. Their real names carry a suffix: `Wave 0: Scaffolding`, `Wave 1: Running Server`, `Wave 2: Auth`, `Wave 3: Identity` AND `Wave 3: Key Sovereignty` (two Wave-3 labels), `Wave 4: Repo + Blobs`, `Wave 5: Federation`, `Wave 6: App Proxy`, `Wave 7: Hardening`, `Wave 8: auth.md`. `save_issue(labels:[...])` matches on the **exact full name** — `labels:["Wave 7"]` silently no-ops (returns `labels:[]`); use `"Wave 7: Hardening"`.

{"additions":376,"author":{"id":"U_kgDOBmYujw","is_bot":false,"login":"malpercio-dev","name":"Malpercio"},"baseRefName":"main","body":"Closes MM-474.

## Why

Every operator-reachable blob figure resolved through `blob_owners`. An account whose ownership rows vanished and one whose files were destroyed reported identical zeroes from the admin listing, per-account storage, `listBlobs`, `listMissingBlobs`, and `getBlob` alike. `blob_scrub` did not cover the class either — its orphan definition is a *file* with no `blobs` row, and the reclaim path deletes the row and the file together, so that walk never sees it.

Telling the two apart meant opening a SQLite shell on the running server.

## What

A second witness at each altitude, both read from the physical table rather than through ownership:

| Surface | Added |
| -- | -- |
| `GET /v1/accounts/:id/storage` | `uploadedBlobCount` / `uploadedBlobBytes` |
| `GET /v1/admin/health` | `blobUnownedCount` / `blobUnownedBytes` |
| `GET /v1/admin/accounts` | `didWebHosting` |

**Per-account** reads `blobs.account_did` — the first-uploader column V039 kept for diagnostics and nothing has read since. Bytes still on disk report here when their ownership rows are gone. It is deliberately the weaker signal: content addressing means a CID uploaded by one account and referenced by another is legitimately owned-not-uploaded, so a gap in either direction is evidence to look at, not a verdict. The doc comments and changelog both say so rather than implying a fault.

**Server-wide** counts `blobs` rows no `blob_owners` row claims. This is the stronger alarm, for a structural reason: `delete_blob_if_unowned` drops the physical row *and* the file together, so a row outlives its owners only for the instant between two statements. ~0 is the true baseline and any standing value is meaningful — no threshold tuning. It is also the one alarm here that fires **without the sweep having stopped**, which is exactly what made the original incident invisible: passes completed on schedule and timestamps stayed fresh throughout.

**`didWebHosting`** is one more correlated scalar in the listing's existing per-row subquery pattern. The opt-in gates a serve path that 404s indistinguishably from an unknown host when off, so an operator could not tell "not hosted" from "broken" without a database shell — load-bearing once it gates did:web sovereign sessions.

## Scope note

The issue's item 2 (a completed pass that skipped work being distinguishable from a clean one) is already covered — `SweepRun::errors` landed with the MM-472 fix in b713a39a and `/v1/admin/health` reports it per sweep. Nothing to add there.

Two naming/shape calls worth flagging for review:

- Named the per-account fields `uploaded*` rather than the issue's "physical". Per-account, "physical" is ambiguous; the column literally records the uploader.
- Did **both** placements the issue offered as alternatives. They answer different questions — "is anything wrong on this server" vs "is this account's data intact" — and neither substitutes for the other.

## Not in this PR

The Brass Console renders none of these yet; they are JSON until the admin-companion account list and Status screen show them. Filed separately, the same way the MM-472 console work became #439.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p pds` — 2218 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy -p pds --all-targets` — clean
- `bruno-parity`, `docs-check`, `ticket-ref-check`, `changelog-check` — green

Six new tests. The load-bearing one deletes the ownership rows out from under a live account and asserts the ownership-scoped view zeroes while the uploader view holds — the exact divergence the readout exists to make visible.

No migration: every column read here already exists (V039's uploader attribution, V044's hosting opt-in).

I've reviewed the full diff and caught the earlier sections too—the changelog entry and AGENTS.md table updates across multiple files. I'm seeing ten files total that were modified: the changelog addition, agent configuration files in different directories, database modules for accounts and blobs, server stats tracking, account storage routes, admin health and account listing endpoints, and the provisioning API spec.

Now I'm analyzing the semantics of the uploader witness field. There's a subtle distinction here: when blob_gc deletes the last owner, it also removes the physical row, so in the actual incident scenario where both ownership rows and physical rows were destroyed, the uploaded blob count would show zero either way. The new metric would actually catch intermediate states—like if only ownership rows were deleted but physical rows remained intact, or during partial restore scenarios—which is different from the complete destruction that happened in the incident. During the diagnosis phase, both physical and ownership counts were zero, so this endpoint would have shown the same zero count, but it would help distinguish between "bytes destroyed" versus "ownership lost."

There's also a limitation worth noting: the `blobs.account_did` field records the first uploader, so after the iCloud restore when the wallet re-uploaded blobs, the account_did would still point to the restoring account—which is fine since it's the same account. For the current live account, the uploaded blob count should align with the total blob count around 540. I'm also reconsidering whether the baseline for unowned blobs is truly near zero—if the upload and ownership operations happen transactionally, unowned blobs would only appear transiently during garbage collection passes, but there are edge cases like shared CIDs where the physical row might exist before a new ownership row is created.

Now I'm thinking through the performance implications of the `blobUnownedCount` query, which does a full table scan with a subquery checking for ownership. If the `blob_owners` table has a primary key on `(account_did, cid)`, then a lookup on just the `cid` column won't use that index efficiently—SQLite would need `cid` as the leading column to optimize the NOT EXISTS probe.

The health endpoint is operator-only and runs infrequently, so even if it's O(blobs × blob_owners) in the worst case, it's acceptable for a small PDS. I should check the V039 migration to see if there's a dedicated index on `cid`.

For the admin listing, the added `did_web_hosting_enabled_at IS NOT NULL` check is just a column read, and SQLite's `IS NOT NULL` expression decodes to a boolean (0/1) through sqlx just fine—the same pattern already used elsewhere.

On the wire compatibility side, the admin-companion parses the `/v1/admin/health` StorageCounts response. For account listing, `deny_unknown_fields` is only set on `RepoRefSubject`, so new fields are tolerated. Bruno parity checks paths only with no new routes, but the PR should verify that response shape changes get documented in the corresponding `.bru` files per the mandatory rule in AGENTS.md.

For docs, the provisioning-api-spec was updated for the storage endpoint, but I need to check whether the admin health and admin accounts endpoints are also documented there — the diff only shows the storage section being modified.

On naming, the `uploaded*` prefix makes sense over "physical". The test coverage looks solid with six new tests hitting db-level divergence, sharing behavior, server stats, route-level storage divergence, health orphans, and didWebHosting listing, plus an existing test update — that covers the incident shape well.

Now checking whether `account_uploaded_blob_metrics` appears in the storage implementation... ## Review: PR #441 — Distinguish blob ownership loss from byte loss (MM-474)

### Overview

Three additive read-side surfaces, no migration: `uploadedBlobCount`/`uploadedBlobBytes` on per-account storage (from `blobs.account_did`, the V039 first-uploader column), `blobUnownedCount`/`blobUnownedBytes` on admin health (physical rows no `blob_owners` row claims), and `didWebHosting` on the account listing. Six tests, spec + AGENTS.md updated. 376 additions, 10 files.

**Correct, and I'd merge after one fix.** Verified independently: the `NOT EXISTS` probe rides `idx_blob_owners_cid` (V039), so no table-scan concern; the admin-companion's health/listing structs are not `deny_unknown_fields` (only `RepoRefSubject` is), so the new fields are wire-safe; `/v1/admin/health` and `/v1/admin/accounts` aren't in provisioning-api-spec.md, so updating only the storage section there is complete, not an omission.

### The design calls are right

- **`uploaded*` over "physical"** — agreed; the column literally records the uploader, and calling it physical would invite reading it as a corrected ownership count, which the doc comments correctly warn against.
- **Both placements** — agreed, and the asymmetry is real: the unowned pair is the *alarm* (baseline ~0 structurally, because `delete_blob_if_unowned` drops row and owner together — no threshold tuning), while the per-account pair is the *diagnostic*. The PR body's observation that the unowned alarm fires without the sweep having stopped is exactly the property the incident lacked.
- The tests hit the precise incident shape — delete ownership rows under a live account, assert the ownership view zeroes while the uploader view holds — plus the benign-sharing direction that keeps the readout from being misread as a fault detector.

### Findings

1. **Bruno response docs are now stale — the repo rule requires updating them** (root AGENTS.md: *"changing any route (…response shape…), update the corresponding `.bru`"*). Three files carry per-field `docs` blocks that no longer match: `account_storage.bru` (missing `uploadedBlobCount`/`uploadedBlobBytes`), `admin_health.bru` (missing `blobUnownedCount`/`blobUnownedBytes`), `admin_list_accounts.bru` (missing `didWebHosting`). `bruno-parity` passed because it checks **paths only** — this is precisely the gap AGENTS.md says the manual rule covers. Only real ask before merge.

2. **One honest-limitation clause worth adding** (nit, doc-comment level): the uploader witness reads 0/0 in the incident's own *end state* too — when blob GC does the destroying, physical rows die with their last owner, so both witnesses zero. What the pair makes HTTP-legible is the *diagnosis*: `owned=0, uploaded>0` → ownership loss; `owned=0, uploaded=0` → bytes gone (the SQL-shell conclusion we drew by hand on 2026-07-25). The current comments describe the first case; one sentence naming the second would stop an operator from reading `uploaded=0` as "nothing was ever here."

3. **Bookkeeping, not this PR:** "Closes MM-474" is right (all three items land: 1 here, 2 via #437's `SweepRun::errors`, 3 here), but #438's outstanding **atrium-repo upstream report** must not be parked on MM-474's checklist or it dies with the close — confirm it has its own ticket.

### Checked and clean

- SQL: user input still bound, never spliced; the new select column follows the `FLAGGED_SQL` derived-bool pattern; `did_web_hosting` isn't part of the sort key or cursor, so pagination is untouched.
- No new routes → no new `.bru` files needed; changelog fragment reads well; no ticket refs in `.rs`/AGENTS.md prose; extra per-request query on an admin-only endpoint is fine.
- The `db/AGENTS.md` `server_stats.rs` row update and the routes-table updates keep the docs honest, including the ~0-baseline reasoning.

**Verdict: approve once the three `.bru` docs blocks are updated (item 1).** Items 2–3 are a nit and a reminder.

One post-merge note for the console follow-up (the PR flags it's JSON-only for now): when the Brass Console renders `blobUnownedCount`, its threshold judgment belongs client-side per the no-verdicts rule — "nonzero across two consecutive sweeps" is the alarm condition the doc comments imply, not "nonzero once," since a value observed mid-pass is legitimately transient.

## So: there is no removal step

The `UPDATE` wrote `temp_until = NULL` — the identical value a legitimate reconcile pin writes. There's no marker to delete, no state to revert, and re-arming clocks by hand would just recreate work reconcile redoes every 30 minutes anyway. The pin didn't need lifting; it dissolved. My earlier "do not lift it blind" caution assumed unreferenced rows were protected *only* by the pin — the 540→532 drop shows reconcile releases them regardless, so that concern is moot.

Two checks, both admin-side (I don't hold the admin token):

1. **The mirror bucket — the one unhealed leg.** The incident deleted the off-volume copies (`deleted bucket object with no blob row` × 534), and the restore only refilled the local volume. `blob_mirror` should have re-uploaded everything since; verify via `/v1/admin/health`'s `blobMirror` sweep entry plus a bucket object count ≈ total physical blobs (or `blob_mirror_synced_total` having jumped by ~500 post-restore). Until that's confirmed, iCloud is still the only second copy — which is the same single-copy exposure the incident started from.

2. **Steady-state health readout**, one glance: `blobGc.errors: 0` holding across passes, `blobUnownedCount: 0`, and on the account's storage endpoint the new `uploadedBlobCount` ≈ `blobCount` (they should roughly agree now; a wild divergence would be the MM-474 signal firing).

Optional third if you want belt-and-braces: `listMissingBlobs` from the wallet's session should return empty — "every record-referenced blob is present," the converse direction of the census I just ran.

description: "2026-07-25 production blob loss on did:web:malpercio.dev — cause, recovery, and the manual DB pin still in place"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: f7424aa7-4556-49e7-b8f5-f9dd85739499
  modified: 2026-07-25T21:55:36.926Z

**2026-07-25:** `did:web:malpercio.dev` lost **534 blobs** on Custos production (`custos-obsign`), recovered from the wallet's iCloud media backup (`restore_blob_backup`). Filed as MM-472 (urgent), MM-473, MM-474, MM-475.

**Cause chain.** NOT data loss — the repo is complete (`sync.getRepo` exports 3.3 MB successfully, and `build_car` reads every record block or errors, so a 200 proves all blocks present). The trigger is MM-473: **atrium-repo 0.1.8 `Node::entries_with_prefix` (mst.rs ~1070)** — a leaf key SHORTER than the prefix makes `key.get(..prefix.len())` return `None`, skipping the comparison and falling through to the unconditional push meant for Tree entries. Leak is governed by key length vs prefix length (NOT node topology; repro = long collection name + one short key like `zz.a/self`). Upstream main still broken as of 2026-07-25, 0.1.8 is latest — no version-bump fix. Sometimes one key leaks, sometimes hundreds (774 for one 5-record collection). Artifacts (frozen CAR + probe output) preserved in gitignored `linear-export/mm-473-artifacts/`. In `list_records_json`, `strip`'s `unwrap_or(key)` keeps the foreign key whole, the re-concatenated `<prefix><foreign-key>` resolves to nothing, and `blob_gc`'s `reconcile_account` throws `repo error: list records: record not found` on every pass. **That `unwrap_or` fallback is load-bearing**: passing the original key through would make `get_raw` succeed and serve foreign records under the wrong collection — fail-closed must be preserved by any fix. Reproducible live: `limit == record_count` → 200 (the bad entry is dropped by `entries.truncate(limit)`), `limit == count+1` → 500. 4 of 78 collections affected. Reconcile is the only thing that pins a blob permanent, and it errors on its first call (`collect_referenced_blob_cids`), so nothing was ever pinned. Phase 2's sweep is **global** and not gated on reconcile success, so 6h after upload (`blobs.temp_ttl_secs` default) it deleted all 534 ownership rows, physical rows, and files. `blob_mirror` then propagated the row deletions to the bucket, destroying the off-volume copy too — iCloud was the last copy.

**LIVE PRODUCTION STATE — pin still in place, now probably redundant.** A manual pin is holding the restored blobs:

```sql
UPDATE blob_owners SET temp_until = NULL WHERE account_did = 'did:web:malpercio.dev';
```

**Update 2026-07-25, v0.8.4 (MM-472 + MM-473 both shipped to prod).** First post-deploy `blob_gc` pass reported `swept 0, errors 0` with `blobCount` steady at 540 — reconcile no longer fails, so those blobs are now pinned on their own merits and the manual pin should be redundant.

**Do NOT lift it blind.** The manual pin and a successful reconcile write the *same* value (`temp_until = NULL`), so inspecting `blob_owners` cannot distinguish "reconcile pinned this" from "the manual UPDATE pinned this". Any restored blob that is owned but NOT referenced by the MST is protected only by the manual pin; lifting re-arms its clock (`temp_ttl_secs`, 6h default) and the next sweep past that window collects it. `repo.listMissingBlobs` does not help — it proves referenced-but-unowned, the opposite direction from the at-risk rows. Resolve via **MM-474** (prod SQLite shell) by diffing the reference set against `blob_owners`, or do a controlled lift and watch `blobCount` across two sweeps while the 6h re-pin window and the iCloud copy are still the floor.

**Gotchas worth keeping:**
- "Visible in bsky" is NOT evidence the PDS holds a blob — `cdn.bsky.app` caches independently and renders long after the origin loses the bytes.
- Every operator-reachable blob read (`admin/accounts` `totalBytes`, `/v1/accounts/:id/storage`, `sync.listBlobs`, `repo.listMissingBlobs`, `sync.getBlob`) reads `blob_owners`. None distinguishes "ownership lost" from "bytes gone" — diagnosis needs a prod SQLite shell (MM-474).
- A `blob_gc` pass with `errors=N` still logs "pass complete" and refreshes its last-run timestamp, so the documented stale-timestamp alarm never fires. Grep WARN `reconcile failed` instead.
- `EZPDS_BLOBS_GC_INTERVAL_SECS=0` is rejected by config validation — not a way to disable GC.

Related: [[project_pds_hostname_migration]], [[project_wallet_icloud_backup_scope]].

# Database Module

Last verified: 2026-07-17

## Latest Updates

- **V057**: Adds `waitlist_signups`, the public interest-signup store behind the `waitlist` capability (`[waitlist] enabled`, off by default): `email` PK (stored normalized via `uniqueness::normalize_email`, so a repeat signup is an idempotent unique-violation no-op rather than a duplicate row or an enumeration oracle), nullable `handle` (optional self-reported atproto handle — syntactically validated by `identity::handle::validate_handle_structure`, deliberately never resolved: it is interest signal, not an authenticated identity claim), `created_at`. **Deliberately no foreign keys**: signups predate any account, so the table stays off the account-purge path entirely (the schema-walking purge test never sees it). Rowid-cursor pagination (V052 doctrine) backs the operator readout. Query functions in `waitlist.rs`; routes in `routes/waitlist_signup.rs` (`POST /waitlist`, public + CORS'd, gated on `[waitlist] enabled`) and `routes/admin_waitlist.rs` (`GET /v1/admin/waitlist`, available regardless of the switch — it reads data already collected).

- **V056**: Adds `pending_oauth_authorizations` + `oauth_consent_audit_events`, the wallet-confirmed OAuth consent primitive (unblocks the sovereign/passwordless lockout where `oauth_authorize.rs` maps a NULL `password_hash` to `WrongPassword`). `pending_oauth_authorizations` is the single-use request the consent page creates in place of the password check: `request_id` PK (high-entropy), unique `user_code` (the distinctly-formatted `XXXX-XXXX` login code from `code_gen::generate_login_code`), a client-metadata snapshot (`client_id` FK→`oauth_clients`, `client_name`) + the full authorization context (redirect_uri, code_challenge[_method], state, response_type, requested_scope), requesting `origin`/`ip`/`user_agent`, optional `login_hint` DID, `status` (CHECK `pending`/`approved`/`denied`/`expired`/`completed`), the bound `account_did` + `granted_scope` set on approval, and `created_at`/`expires_at` (~5-min TTL). **Derived-status doctrine:** `expired` is computed from `expires_at` at read time, not persisted — no background sweep; lapsed rows are reclaimed opportunistically on the next creation (`cleanup_expired_pending_authorizations`, the `oauth_par_requests`/`transfers` precedent). Terminal transitions are guarded single-statement UPDATEs (`approve`/`deny`/`complete`), so a replayed device-key approval envelope lands on an already-terminal row and wins nothing — the envelope's `request_id` binding + this single-use row together subsume a nonce store. `account_did` is deliberately **not** an `accounts` FK (ephemeral row, DID already verified against authoritative PLC at approval; keeps the table off the account-purge path, like `agent_child_deletions.child_did`). `oauth_consent_audit_events` is append-only in the `agent_audit_events` (V040) / `admin_audit_events` (V052) mold (INSERT+SELECT only, rowid-cursor, **no FKs** so the trail outlives its ephemeral row + subject): `request_created`/`approved`/`denied`/`completed`, `detail` mechanical facts only. Query functions in `pending_oauth_authorizations.rs`; routes in `routes/oauth_consent.rs` (`GET /oauth/authorize/consent-request` wallet preview, `GET /oauth/authorize/status` slow_down-throttled poll, `POST /oauth/authorize/approve` device-key-signed, `POST /oauth/authorize/complete` code issuance) plus the wallet path added to `routes/oauth_authorize.rs`'s `get_authorization`.

- **V055**: Drops `pending_accounts.pending_share_{1,2,3}` (MM-426) — the retired server-side DID ceremony's idempotent share store. V011 added these so the pre-inversion `POST /v1/dids` path could return the same three Shamir shares across retries (avoiding an orphaned Share 2 in `accounts.recovery_share`). The ceremony inversion (MM-407) moved share generation client-side, and MM-426 retires the legacy server-side path entirely: a did:plc request now *requires* the wallet's `recoveryKey` + `escrowShare` (400 otherwise), the server never generates or splits a secret, and did:web promotes with no escrow. Nothing reads or writes these columns anymore — they only ever put two-of-three reconstruction material into Litestream backups. Forward-only `DROP COLUMN` (SQLite ≥ 3.35): plain nullable TEXT, no index/FK/default, so it applies cleanly on a populated `pending_accounts`. `pending_did` (V008) and `pending_plc_registered_at` (V054) stay — they gate the share-independent DID-pre-store / plc.directory re-POST retry logic. `accounts.recovery_share` (V010) is untouched (dropped later by the old-account re-key migration, MM-411).

- **V054**: Adds nullable `pending_plc_registered_at` TEXT to `pending_accounts` (MM-424) — the confirmed-PLC-registration marker the DID ceremony (`routes/create_did.rs`, `POST /v1/dids`) reads on a retry. `pending_did` (V008) was overloaded as proof of a completed plc.directory registration, but it is pre-stored *before* the `post_to_plc_directory` POST, so a retry after a **failed** POST saw it set, took the skip-plc branch, and promoted a DID that may never have registered globally (an "active" account whose DID doesn't resolve on the network — handle resolution/federation/PLC-monitoring silently fail later). This column is stamped (`mark_plc_registered`, `datetime('now')`) only *after* a 2xx from plc.directory; the retry branch (`pre_store_did` for the client-share path, `pre_store_did_and_shares` for the legacy path) skips the POST only when it is set and otherwise re-POSTs the idempotent signed genesis op (same op → same DID). Share reuse stays gated on `pending_did` as before — the two decisions are orthogonal (shares stay stable while the POST retries). Stamped before the promotion transaction, so a retry whose promotion failed still skips the (already-done) POST; dropped with the `pending_accounts` row at promotion, like `pending_did`. Derived-status doctrine (NULL = not yet confirmed). No writer/reader outside `create_did.rs`.

- **V053**: Adds `recovery_otps`, the email-OTP store gating the escrow-assisted recovery *release* flow (MM-409). Same SHA-256-hashed, 1-hour, single-use envelope as `password_reset_tokens` (V014) / `plc_operation_tokens` (V033) / `account_deletion_tokens` (V034) / `email_tokens` (V036): `token_hash` PK, `did` FK→`accounts`, `expires_at`, nullable `used_at`, `created_at`, plus `idx_recovery_otps_did`. `POST /v1/recovery/initiate` mints one (always-200, no enumeration — the `requestPasswordReset` posture) and the opening `POST /v1/recovery/release` call consumes it (atomic single-use, bound to `(token_hash, did)` so it can neither be replayed nor spent against another account). A dedicated table (not a new `purpose` on an existing one) keeps the recovery credential from ever being redeemable in another flow. Query functions in `recovery_otps.rs`; `account_delete::purge_account` deletes these rows. The release *state machine* rides V050's existing `recovery_escrow.release_requested_at`/`release_pending_until` columns (written now, for the first time, by the release flow) and appends `release_requested`/`release_cancelled`/`released` rows to `recovery_audit_events` (the vocabulary V050's CHECK already reserved).

- **V052**: Adds `admin_audit_events`, the **server-wide** append-only admin action audit log (MM-283) — the unified answer to "what have admins done on this relay?". One row per privileged mutating admin action: `actor` (the `AdminActor` log string — `master-token` / `device:<id>`, plus `pairing-code` for device enrollments, whose acting credential is the consumed code, not an existing admin identity), `action` (typed vocabulary in `admin_audit.rs::AdminAuditAction` — takedown/restore, credential sweep, claim-code mint/revoke, pairing-code mint, device register/revoke, transfer cancel, request-crawl, email repair, reset-token issuance, signing-key creation), nullable `subject` (account DID / device id / transfer id / claim code), `outcome`, and a `detail` JSON of mechanical facts (counts, resulting status — never codes or token material). **Deliberately no foreign keys**: the trail must outlive its subjects (a takedown row survives the account's permanent deletion; `purge_account` touches nothing here), unlike the account-scoped `operator_account_audit_events` (V046), which the repair routes now double-write alongside. Only real state transitions are recorded — idempotent repeats (re-revoking a revoked device) write nothing. Writes join the mutating route's transaction where one exists; everywhere a failed audit write fails the request (fail closed — a privileged action must not land unattributed). Rowid-cursor pagination (V040 doctrine) plus `action`/`actor`/`subject` equality indexes back `GET /v1/admin/audit` (`routes/admin_audit.rs`) and the Brass Console's Audit screen. Queries in `admin_audit.rs`.

- **V051**: Adds `account_labels` (WITHOUT ROWID, PK `(did, labeler_did, val)`, FK→`accounts(did)`, `idx_account_labels_labeler`), the watched-labeler flag store behind the operator triage view: one row per account-level label *currently in force* from a `[labeler] watched` labeler, reconciled each `labeler_watch.rs` pass (a negated/expired label's row is deleted, not tombstoned — the table is an explicitly rebuildable cache of external labeler state, unlike the derived-status doctrine tables). `cts` is the labeler's creation timestamp (shown to the operator); `first_seen_at` records first local observation — the seam a future push-notifier uses to tell a genuinely new flag from backfill. Query functions in `account_labels.rs`; the listing-side predicates (`FLAGGED_SQL` flagged-first ordering + composite cursor, `count_accounts_admin_flagged`) live in `accounts.rs`. `account_delete::purge_account` deletes these account-owned rows before `accounts` (no FK cascade, as ever).

- **V050**: Adds the escrow storage for the one Shamir share Custos holds under the client-generated share model: `recovery_escrow` (WITHOUT ROWID, `did` PK FK→`accounts`; `share_encrypted` is the 42-byte v2 share envelope AES-256-GCM-wrapped under the master KEK from day one — registered as `SecretFamily::RecoveryEscrow` in `kek.rs`, so `pds rewrap-master-key` covers it via the generic-length `crypto::{encrypt,decrypt}_secret_bytes` pair; `rotated_at` NULL = never replaced, `release_requested_at`/`release_pending_until` NULL = no release in flight — derived-status doctrine, written only by the escrow release flow) and `recovery_audit_events` (append-only, the `agent_audit_events` V040 doctrine: INSERT/SELECT only, rowid cursors, `purge_account` the sole remover; a CHECK constraint reserves the full event vocabulary — `deposited`/`rotated`/`deleted` written by the owner endpoints, `release_requested`/`release_cancelled`/`released` reserved for the release flow; `detail` carries mechanical facts only, never share material). Query functions in `recovery_escrow.rs` and `recovery_audit.rs`; wired by `routes/recovery_escrow.rs` (`PUT`/`DELETE /v1/recovery/escrow-share`) and by `routes/create_did.rs`' client-share ceremony path (the genesis-time deposit + `deposited` audit event land inside the promotion transaction). The legacy `accounts.recovery_share` column (V010) is deliberately untouched — it is dropped by the old-account re-key migration once existing accounts move to the new model.
- **V049**: Adds `agent_child_deletions`, the durable tombstone for a parent's deletion of a sovereign child agent (MM-400). Deleting a child reuses the deactivate + `delete_after` + reaper pipeline, so the reaper eventually calls `account_delete::purge_account`, which drops the child's account, repo, handle, blobs, `agent_identities` row *and* its whole `agent_audit_events` trail — the child's own history cannot outlive it. This table is the V030-style anchor for "the deletion is auditable after the fact": keyed by `child_did` with **no FK to `accounts` on that column** so a child purge leaves it intact, but with `parent_did REFERENCES accounts(did)` so the parent's audit view outlives the child. `purge_account` deletes it `WHERE parent_did = ?` (reclaimed when the *parent* is deleted), **never** `WHERE child_did = ?`. `handle`/`registration_id` are denormalized because their source rows are purged with the child. Queries in `agent_child_deletions.rs`.
- **V047**: Rebuilds `agent_identities` for sovereign child agents (nullable-`parent_did` + `child` registration type, plus the new `agent_child_provisionings` table). **Rebuild invariant, learned the hard way (v0.5.1's production deploy failed on this):** dropping the old parent implicit-deletes its rows while child FKs still reference the table name, so *every* table with an FK into `agent_identities (id)` must be cycled through a temp stash around the swap — `agent_claim_attempts` (V037) *and* `agent_audit_events` (V040). The audit stash carries rowids explicitly (`CREATE TABLE AS SELECT` drops them; the audit trail's pagination cursors are rowid-based). A fresh-DB migration run can't catch a missed child (the tables are empty), so any future parent-table rebuild needs a populated-upgrade-path test like `v047_rebuild_preserves_audit_events_and_claim_attempts` / `v038_rebuild_preserves_child_rows_and_allows_null_did` in `mod.rs`.

- **V046**: Adds `operator_account_audit_events`, the durable audit trail for admin account repair. `email_updated` records the authenticated admin actor plus previous/new normalized addresses; `reset_token_issued` records issuance without token material (refused with 400 for a passwordless account, so no token or audit row is written — a key-sovereign account is recovered through its escrowed key share, not a password reset). Both writes are atomic with their repair operation, and permanent account deletion removes these account-owned rows before deleting `accounts`.

- **V045**: Normalizes existing `accounts.email` / `pending_accounts.email` rows to lowercase (trimmed) in place — a data-only migration, no schema change. Both columns already carry a UNIQUE index (`idx_accounts_email` / `idx_pending_accounts_email`), so the normalizing `UPDATE` fails loudly (aborting the whole migration transaction) if two rows would collide once normalized, rather than silently merging them; an operator must resolve the collision manually before the migration can apply. Pairs with the normalize-on-every-read/write-path fix in `uniqueness.rs` (`normalize_email`, shared by `email_taken`) and `accounts.rs` (`resolve_by_email`, `update_account_email`) — the reference PDS lowercases emails on store and lookup, and without this the account-creation routes' byte-exact matching let a differently-cased signup email silently fail later matches (e.g. `requestPasswordReset` 200-and-no-op with no way to discover the mismatch).
- **V044**: Adds nullable `did_web_hosting_enabled_at` TEXT to `accounts` — the opt-in flag for Custos-managed did:web hosting (MM-279). Derived-status doctrine (V008/V026/V004): NULL = hosting off (never enabled or turned back off); a timestamp = when it was last enabled. The `.well-known/did.json` serve route (`routes/did_json.rs`) reads through this column joined to `did_documents` and the active-lifecycle gate (`dids::serve_hosted_did_document`), so an account that isn't opted in 404s exactly like an unknown host — no opt-in existence oracle. did:plc accounts never set it (their document lives on plc.directory). Writers/readers in `dids.rs`: `set_did_web_hosting` (toggle), `did_web_hosting_enabled` (probe), `serve_hosted_did_document` (gated serve). The opt-in toggle + the authenticated non-PLC document-edit path (direct `did_documents` overwrite via `rewrite_did_document` + `#identity` firehose frame) live in `routes/did_web_hosting.rs`.
- **V043**: Adds `sovereign_session_nonces`, a dedicated DID-scoped anti-replay store for sovereign-session signed requests. Its `(did, nonce)` primary key makes insert-if-absent atomic and permits the same random nonce across different identities; the DID FK binds rows to hosted accounts, and `idx_sovereign_session_nonces_seen_at` supports bounded stale-row cleanup. The query layer rejects a retention threshold at or below the full `2 * SOVEREIGN_TIMESTAMP_WINDOW_SECS` replay-acceptance span, so sweeping cannot reopen a replay while its signed timestamp is still acceptable. It deliberately does not reuse `admin_nonces`, whose rows are owned by admin device ids.
- **V042**: Seeds the identity wallet's **canonical** OAuth client row: client_id `https://identitywallet.obsign.org/oauth/client-metadata.json` with redirect URI `org.obsign.identitywallet:/oauth/callback` — the reverse-FQDN scheme⇄host pairing the atproto OAuth spec requires for a native client's private-use redirect (and third-party AS's like bsky.social enforce; the PAR handler now enforces it too for discoverable clients). The wallet's OAuth identity is this fixed URL (it no longer varies with the configured Custos); seeding the row lets any instance accept the wallet without an outbound fetch of the canonical document. Uses `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` (corrects a previously cached copy). The V013 row is deliberately kept so pre-transition wallet builds (old client_id + old scheme) keep working. The client-metadata route (`routes/oauth_client_metadata.rs`) serves the same canonical document, with a loopback-`public_url` exception for local dev.
- **Operator transfer visibility/cancel** (no new migration — extends V027/V029/V030 semantics): `transfers.status` gains a new **terminal** value, `cancelled` (operator interruption). No schema change is needed: the column is unconstrained TEXT, and both partial UNIQUE indexes (`idx_transfers_active_did`/`idx_transfers_active_code`) enumerate the *active* statuses, so a cancelled row frees the per-DID and per-code slots exactly like `complete`/`expired`, and every accept/complete lookup (which filters on the active list) ignores it. `transfers.rs` gains `list_inflight_transfers` (the operator view: `accepted`/`completing` rows regardless of expiry — completion has no expiry predicate, so a lapsed accepted transfer can still finish — plus unexpired `pending`; `(created_at, id)` keyset pages; deliberately never selects `code`, a live account-takeover credential), `mark_transfer_cancelled` (UPDATE guarded on the active statuses), and `revoke_transfer_device` (single-credential `revoked_at` tombstone, V030 doctrine). The cross-table cancel transaction (sweep-if-lapsed → cancel → tombstone accepted credential → `transfer.cancelled` audit event) lives in the root `transfer.rs::cancel_transfer`, backing `GET /v1/admin/transfers` + `POST /v1/admin/transfers/{id}/cancel` (`routes/admin_transfers.rs`).
- **V041**: Adds nullable `revoked_at` TEXT to `claim_codes` plus a composite `(created_at, code)` index — operator revocation for a minted-but-unredeemed claim code (a live signup credential). Derived-status doctrine (V004/V025): NULL = never revoked; every redemption path (the atomic single-use UPDATEs in `register_device.rs`/`create_account_xrpc.rs`/`create_mobile_account.rs` and the `claim_code_valid` preflight) additionally requires `revoked_at IS NULL`, so revocation closes redemption exactly like expiry, and the row survives as the audit record. Deliberately an in-place ALTER, not a rebuild: `pending_accounts.claim_code` (V005) FK-references `claim_codes (code)`, so a DROP/rename rebuild fails on any DB holding pending rows; the inventory therefore pages on the immutable `(created_at, code)` keyset (stable across VACUUM — this TEXT-keyed table's implicit rowid is not). `claim_codes.rs` gains `list_claim_codes` (newest-first keyset page, `is_expired` evaluated in SQL so "now" is derived once) and `revoke_claim_code` (guarded UPDATE `redeemed_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL`; a failed attempt is classified race-free into `AlreadyRevoked`/`Redeemed`/`NotFound` because those states are terminal). Backing `GET /v1/accounts/claim-codes` + `POST /v1/accounts/claim-codes/revoke` (admin companion's inventory screen).
- **V040**: Adds `agent_audit_events`, the **append-only** agent-action audit log (`id`, `registration_id` FK→`agent_identities`, nullable `did` FK→`accounts` — NULL for pre-claim events on an ownerless anonymous registration —, `event_type`, `detail` JSON, `created_at`; indexes on `(registration_id, created_at)` and `(did, created_at)`). Modeled on `transfer_audit_events` (V030): the query layer (`agent_audit.rs`) exposes INSERT and SELECT only — no UPDATE/DELETE exists or may be added; `account_delete::purge_account` is the sole remover (keyed through the identity — `registration_id IN (SELECT id FROM agent_identities WHERE did = ?)` — because NULL-did events still pin the identity row via the FK, ordered before the `agent_claim_attempts`/`agent_identities` deletes). Event vocabulary is the `AgentAuditEventType` enum (`registered`, `claim_initiated`, `claim_confirmed`, `claim_expired`, `token_exchanged`, `repo_write`, `blob_upload`, `revoked`); `detail` carries mechanical facts only (op counts, collections, mime/size, grant kind) — never record bodies, user codes, or token material. Pagination cursors on the table's rowid (append-only ⇒ rowid order = event order). Writers: registration + claim routes, the token endpoint, `record_write::commit_repo_write` (atomically with the CAS), `upload_blob`, the `/v1/agents` revoke route, and the `agent_claim_sweep` background pass.
- **V039**: Adds `blob_owners`, the authoritative per-account ownership/lifecycle table for globally content-addressed blobs — the blob counterpart of V035's `block_owners`, fixing the shared-blob destruction bug (one account's GC/deletion destroying a file another account's records still reference). `blobs` is rebuilt down to physical metadata (cid, first-uploader `account_did` for diagnostics only — FK to accounts removed —, mime/size/path); `ref_count` and `temp_until` move onto `blob_owners` (PK `(account_did, cid)`, FK→`accounts` (NO ACTION — `purge_account` deletes ownership rows explicitly) + FK→`blobs` (ON DELETE CASCADE)), so each owner has its own reference count and grace clock. `insert_blob` upserts both rows (a re-upload restarts *that account's* grace clock only while its `ref_count` is 0); every account-scoped query (`getBlob`'s `get_owned_blob`, quota/metrics, `listBlobs`, `present_cids`, `account_last_active`) reads through `blob_owners`; blob GC (`blob_gc.rs`) reconciles per owner — walking every account that owns blobs *or has a repo*, adopting referenced-but-unowned stored CIDs into `blob_owners` (which heals pre-V039 implicit sharing, so no `legacy_protected` flag is needed: adoption runs before any sweep) — and the sweep expires owner rows individually, deleting the physical row + file only when the last owner is gone (`delete_blob_if_unowned`, single-statement guard). `account_delete::purge_account` uses `delete_owners_and_unowned_blobs_in_tx`, mirroring the block path: a CID another account still owns keeps its row and file.
- **V038**: Rebuilds `agent_identities` to make `did` **nullable** so the auth.md `anonymous` flow can register an ownerless identity (a `NULL` did = no owning account until a later claim ceremony binds one); the FK to `accounts(did)` still applies to non-NULL values. SQLite can't drop a column's NOT NULL in place, so the table is rebuilt. `PRAGMA foreign_keys` can't be toggled mid-transaction and `defer_foreign_keys` leaves an unbalanced deferred-violation counter across the parent drop/rename (dropping the old parent implicit-deletes its rows while `agent_claim_attempts(identity_id)` still references the table name), so the child rows are cycled through a temp stash — emptied before the parent swap and refilled after — keeping FK enforcement on with no orphan window. `agent_auth.rs`'s `NewAgentIdentity.did`/`AgentIdentityRow.did` become `Option`, and the jwt-bearer exchange (`oauth_token.rs`) compares the stored did against the assertion `sub` as an `Option` (a NULL-did anonymous identity is never `claimed`, so it never exchanges).
- **V037**: Adds the auth.md agent-registration state tables: `agent_identities` (FK→`accounts.did`, registration type, issuer/subject/email metadata, granted scopes JSON, service assertion material, optional claim token, active/claimed/revoked status) and `agent_claim_attempts` (FK→`agent_identities.id`, 6-digit user code, expiry, target email, pending/completed/expired status). Query functions live in `agent_auth.rs` and intentionally keep JWT validation/code generation in future route code.
- **V036**: Adds the `email_tokens` table (same SHA-256-hashed, 1-hour, single-use envelope as `password_reset_tokens` V014 / `plc_operation_tokens` V033 / `account_deletion_tokens` V034), with a `purpose` column (`confirm`|`update`) so one table backs both the `confirmEmail` and `updateEmail` flows without a token from one being redeemable in the other. `requestEmailConfirmation`/`requestEmailUpdate` insert a token (delivered via the outbound-email path); `confirmEmail`/`updateEmail` consume it (bound to `(token_hash, did, purpose)`, atomic single-use). Query functions live in `email_tokens.rs`; the confirmation-state writers `set_email_confirmed` (sets `email_confirmed_at`) and `update_account_email` (changes `email` + clears `email_confirmed_at`, reporting an `idx_accounts_email` UNIQUE collision as `Taken`) live in `accounts.rs`. This is the first migration to accompany a real outbound-email sender (`pds/src/email.rs`, `[email]` config) rather than the logged-token stub the earlier token tables shipped with.
- **V035**: Adds `block_owners`, the authoritative per-account ownership/revision table for globally content-addressed repo blocks. `blocks` still stores physical bytes once by CID, but its legacy `account_did` FK is removed during a table rebuild so account deletion no longer has to delete shared global bytes. Existing physical rows are marked `legacy_protected` because historic implicit shared references cannot be reconstructed in SQL. Repo writes insert/update both `blocks` and `block_owners`; account-scoped reads/stats/incremental-export/GC use `block_owners`; GC and account deletion remove ownership rows and reclaim only unowned, non-legacy physical bytes.
- **V034**: Adds the `account_deletion_tokens` table (same SHA-256-hashed, 1-hour, single-use envelope as `plc_operation_tokens` V033 / `password_reset_tokens` V014): email tokens gating `com.atproto.server.deleteAccount`. `requestAccountDelete` inserts a token (delivery stubbed → logged, pending an outbound-email path); `deleteAccount` consumes it (bound to `(token_hash, did)`, atomic single-use). Query functions live in `account_deletion_tokens.rs`. **Permanent-deletion note:** **no account-keyed FK cascades** — the only `ON DELETE CASCADE` in the schema hangs content-addressed ownership rows off their physical tables (`block_owners.cid`→`blocks`, `blob_owners.cid`→`blobs` since V039), never off `accounts` — so account deletion (`account_delete::purge_account`, shared by `deleteAccount` and the `deleteAfter` reaper) must delete every child row explicitly in FK order, never relying on cascade behavior (`refresh_tokens`→`sessions`; `transfer_audit_events`→`transfers`→`transfer_devices`; then the rest), reclaims on-disk blob files no other account owns (per `blob_owners`, V039), and emits an `#account` (`active=false`, `status="deleted"`) frame — but deliberately leaves `repo_seq` untouched (punching per-DID holes would break cursor-replay density), removes repo block ownership rows without deleting shared global block bytes, and does **not** tombstone the did:plc identity (the PDS holds no rotation key; ADR-0001).
- **V033**: Adds the `plc_operation_tokens` table (same SHA-256-hashed, 1-hour, single-use envelope as `password_reset_tokens` V014): email tokens that authorize `com.atproto.identity.signPlcOperation` on the interop account-migration path (ADR-0002). `requestPlcOperationSignature` inserts a token (delivery stubbed → logged, pending an outbound-email path); `signPlcOperation` consumes it. Only the plaintext's hash is stored; `consume_plc_operation_token` marks it used in one statement bound to `(token_hash, did)` so it can neither be replayed nor spent by another account. Query functions live in `plc_operation_tokens.rs`.
- **V032**: Adds the `reserved_signing_keys` table for `com.atproto.server.reserveSigningKey`: public account-migration clients can reserve a repo signing `did:key` before the destination account row exists. The table stores the encrypted PDS-held private key using the same AES-256-GCM envelope as other signing-key storage; `did` is nullable but UNIQUE when provided, making DID-keyed reservations idempotent while allowing anonymous reservations to be claimed later by returned `id`. Query functions live in `repo_keys.rs`.
- **Takedown enforcement + admin surface** (no new migration — reuses V026's columns): `accounts.rs::set_account_takedown` is the first writer for `taken_down_at`, backing `com.atproto.admin.updateSubjectStatus`/`getSubjectStatus` (`routes/update_subject_status.rs`, `routes/get_subject_status.rs`, admin-authed). The lifecycle-gated lookups that previously keyed on `deactivated_at` alone (`get_session_account`, `resolve_identifier`, `resolve_by_email`, `get_repo_write_state`, `advance_repo_root_if_active`) now also require `suspended_at`/`taken_down_at` IS NULL, so a suspension or takedown closes logins and repo writes exactly like a self-service deactivation — closing the enforcement gap V026 left open.
- **V031**: Adds the `app_passwords` table (WITHOUT ROWID, keyed by `(did, name)`, FK→`accounts`): named credentials for the legacy `createSession` flow. Each row stores the argon2id hash of a generated secret (plaintext surfaced once at creation, never stored) plus a `privileged` flag mirroring atproto's `com.atproto.appPass` vs `com.atproto.appPassPrivileged` scopes. `createSession` verifies a supplied password against the account's app-password hashes when the main password does not match (and for mobile accounts with no main password), issuing an app-pass-scoped access token and tagging the refresh token's dormant `app_password_name` column (introduced V002, rebuilt into the live schema by V006); `refreshSession` reads that column to keep the rotated session app-pass-scoped, and refuses to rotate if the app password has since been revoked. Revocation deletes the row *and* the app password's refresh tokens/sessions. Query functions live in `app_passwords.rs`; the revocation transaction lives in `routes/revoke_app_password.rs`.
- **V030**: Adds transfer completion audit metadata for planned device swaps. `transfers.completed_at` records when an accepted transfer becomes terminal, and `transfer_audit_events` stores an immutable event row for completion. The completion workflow keeps the accepted target `transfer_devices` credential, marks prior transfer-device credentials revoked, deletes all promoted account sessions/refresh tokens for the DID, and writes one audit row in the same transaction.
- **V028**: Adds the `repo_seq` table — the **persistent firehose event log** backing
  `com.atproto.sync.subscribeRepos`. The sequencer (`firehose.rs`) was in-memory only, so `seq`
  reset to 0 and the replay backlog emptied on every restart/redeploy. Each sequenced event (a
  `#commit`, `#account`, `#identity`, or `#sync` frame) is now persisted here *before* being broadcast, so `seq` is
  monotonic across restarts (loaded from `MAX(seq)` on boot) and cursor replay reads missed events
  back out of the log. `seq` is an explicit `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` (rowid alias for index-backed
  `seq > ?` scans) assigned by the in-process sequencer — **not** `AUTOINCREMENT` — so a failed
  insert doesn't consume a number and leave a hole in the dense prefix replay relies on. `event` is
  the DAG-CBOR payload that reconstructs the wire frame, including the commit's CARv1 `blocks`
  (stored because post-commit GC may have reclaimed the blocks the diff was built from); the record
  `value` is not stored (not on the wire). Append-only at the writer, but bounded by the
  `firehose_gc` retention sweep (`run_firehose_gc` prunes a contiguous prefix `seq ≤ watermark`,
  never the live frontier; `retained_boundary_seq`/`prune_below` do the SQL). Query functions live in
  `firehose_seq.rs`.
- **V027**: Adds the `transfers` table for planned device-swap sessions (`POST /v1/transfer/initiate` and the later accept/complete steps). State machine `pending → accepted → completing → complete`, plus a terminal `expired`. One active transfer per account is enforced by a partial UNIQUE index `idx_transfers_active_did ON transfers(did) WHERE status IN ('pending','accepted','completing')`. Expiry is **not** in the index predicate (SQLite requires deterministic predicates; `datetime('now')` is not), so `transfers.rs::insert_transfer` sweeps any expired active row to `expired` before inserting — a still-active row then trips the index and is reported as `DuplicateActive` (the 409 path). A second partial UNIQUE index `idx_transfers_active_code ON transfers(code) WHERE status IN ('pending','accepted','completing')` keeps the 6-char code (the accept-time lookup key) unique among active transfers; an INSERT that trips it is reported as `CodeCollision`, and `routes/transfer_initiate.rs` regenerates the code and retries (bounded). The two cases are told apart via `unique_violation_column`. FK→`accounts(did)`.
- **V026**: Adds nullable `suspended_at` and `taken_down_at` TEXT columns to `accounts` — the moderation-lifecycle signals `com.atproto.sync.getRepoStatus`/`listRepos` report beyond user-initiated `deactivated_at`. Status is derived, not stored (matching `deactivated_at`/`claim_codes`): `accounts.rs::AccountLifecycle::from_timestamps` collapses the three timestamps to `Active`/`Deactivated`/`Suspended`/`TakenDown` with precedence takendown > suspended > deactivated, feeding `get_repo_status` (handler maps the state to the lexicon `active`/`status`) and `list_repos`' `active` flag. The writer (`set_account_takedown`, backing `com.atproto.admin.updateSubjectStatus`) and full enforcement (repo-write gate, login/session lookups) landed later — see "Takedown enforcement + admin surface" above.
- **V025**: Adds the admin-device data model for the operator companion app — three tables: `admin_pairing_codes` (single-use, short-TTL enrollment codes), `admin_devices` (per-device public keys as `did:key`, with a `scopes` growth hook defaulting to `full`), and `admin_nonces` (seen request nonces for anti-replay, keyed `(device_id, nonce)` so uniqueness is per-device, FK→`admin_devices`). Status is derived, not stored (matching `claim_codes` V004): a pairing code is *pending* while `consumed_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now`; a device is *active* while `revoked_at IS NULL`. Query functions live in `admin_devices.rs`; the pairing/register routes (`routes/admin_devices.rs`) wire the mint/get/consume + insert functions. The signed-request guard (`require_admin` in `auth/guards.rs`) consumes `get_device`/`insert_nonce_if_absent`/`touch_last_seen` (the last bumps `last_seen_at` on a successful device auth). The list/revoke device-management routes (`routes/admin_devices.rs`: `GET /v1/admin/devices`, `POST /v1/admin/devices/:id/revoke`) consume `list_devices`/`revoke_device`/`get_device`.
- **V024**: Adds nullable `delete_after` TEXT column to `accounts` — records the optional `deleteAfter` instant from `com.atproto.server.deactivateAccount` (a requested permanent-deletion time). Set alongside `deactivated_at` on deactivation and cleared on reactivation; the reaper that acts on it is not yet implemented. `deactivated_at` (V008) records *that* an account is deactivated; this records *when it asked to be deleted*.
- **V023**: Adds `account_preferences` table (WITHOUT ROWID, keyed by `did`): a single JSON blob per account holding the user's `app.bsky` preferences array, stored locally on the PDS (user data sovereignty) instead of being proxied to the AppView. `updated_at` tracks the last write; FK→`accounts(did)`.
- **V022**: Adds `iroh_identity` table (WITHOUT ROWID, single-row, keyed by UUID id) storing the PDS's Iroh node Ed25519 secret key, AES-256-GCM encrypted with the signing-key master key (same scheme as `oauth_signing_key` (V012) and `jwt_signing_secret` (V015)). Keeps the PDS's Iroh node id stable across restarts.
- **V014**: Adds `password_reset_tokens` table: `token_hash` TEXT PK (SHA-256 hex digest — plaintext never stored), `did` TEXT (FK→accounts), `expires_at` TEXT (1-hour TTL, SQLite datetime), `used_at` TEXT nullable (set on consumption), `created_at` TEXT; index on `did`
- **V013**: Seeds the identity-wallet as a registered OAuth client (`dev.malpercio.identitywallet`) with native application type, DPoP-bound tokens, and custom URL scheme redirect URI (`dev.malpercio.identitywallet:/oauth/callback`); uses INSERT OR IGNORE for idempotency
- **V012**: Adds nullable `jkt` TEXT column to `oauth_tokens` (DPoP key thumbprint for DPoP-bound refresh tokens); creates `oauth_signing_key` table (WITHOUT ROWID, single-row, stores the server's persistent ES256 keypair with AES-256-GCM-encrypted private key)

## Purpose
Owns SQLite connection lifecycle and schema migration for the PDS's server-level database.
Keeps database concerns out of handler code and provides a reusable pool+migration API
that can later serve per-user SQLite databases (Wave 3/4).

## Contracts
- **Exposes**: `open_pool(url: &str) -> Result<SqlitePool, DbError>`, `run_migrations(pool: &SqlitePool) -> Result<(), DbError>`, `DbError`
- **Guarantees**: Pool uses WAL journal mode and max 1 connection. The schema_migrations bootstrap DDL runs outside any transaction. Pending migrations and their bookkeeping inserts run inside a single transaction per call. Migrations are forward-only and idempotent. `schema_migrations` table tracks applied versions.
- **Expects**: Valid sqlx SQLite URL (e.g. `"sqlite::memory:"`, `"sqlite:path.db"`). Pool must be open before calling `run_migrations`.

## Dependencies
- **Uses**: sqlx (SqlitePool, SqliteConnectOptions), thiserror
- **Used by**: `main.rs` (startup sequence), `app::AppState` (holds the pool), test helpers
- **Boundary**: Handlers never call `open_pool`/`run_migrations` directly; they receive the pool via `AppState.db`

## Key Decisions
- Custom migration runner over sqlx's built-in `migrate!()`: gives control over transaction boundaries and avoids sqlx's `_sqlx_migrations` table
- Single connection pool (`max_connections(1)`): avoids SQLite write contention, sufficient for v0.1
- `open_pool` accepts `&str` (not Config/AppState): keeps the function reusable for future per-user DBs

## Invariants
- Migration SQL files are append-only; never modify an applied migration
- Migration versions are sequential positive integers starting at 1
- WAL mode is always enabled (set via SqliteConnectOptions, not raw PRAGMA)
- Foreign key enforcement is always on (set via SqliteConnectOptions .foreign_keys(true), not raw PRAGMA)

**2026-07-25:** `did:web:malpercio.dev` lost **534 blobs** on Custos production (`custos-obsign`), recovered from the wallet's iCloud media backup (`restore_blob_backup`). Filed as MM-472 (urgent), MM-473, MM-474, MM-475.

**Cause chain.** NOT data loss — the repo is complete (`sync.getRepo` exports 3.3 MB successfully, and `build_car` reads every record block or errors, so a 200 proves all blocks present). The trigger is MM-473: **atrium-repo 0.1.8 `Node::entries_with_prefix` (mst.rs ~1070)** — a leaf key SHORTER than the prefix makes `key.get(..prefix.len())` return `None`, skipping the comparison and falling through to the unconditional push meant for Tree entries. Leak is governed by key length vs prefix length (NOT node topology; repro = long collection name + one short key like `zz.a/self`). Upstream main still broken as of 2026-07-25, 0.1.8 is latest — no version-bump fix. Sometimes one key leaks, sometimes hundreds (774 for one 5-record collection). Artifacts (frozen CAR + probe output) preserved in gitignored `linear-export/mm-473-artifacts/`. In `list_records_json`, `strip`'s `unwrap_or(key)` keeps the foreign key whole, the re-concatenated `<prefix><foreign-key>` resolves to nothing, and `blob_gc`'s `reconcile_account` throws `repo error: list records: record not found` on every pass. **That `unwrap_or` fallback is load-bearing**: passing the original key through would make `get_raw` succeed and serve foreign records under the wrong collection — fail-closed must be preserved by any fix. Reproducible live: `limit == record_count` → 200 (the bad entry is dropped by `entries.truncate(limit)`), `limit == count+1` → 500. 4 of 78 collections affected. Reconcile is the only thing that pins a blob permanent, and it errors on its first call (`collect_referenced_blob_cids`), so nothing was ever pinned. Phase 2's sweep is **global** and not gated on reconcile success, so 6h after upload (`blobs.temp_ttl_secs` default) it deleted all 534 ownership rows, physical rows, and files. `blob_mirror` then propagated the row deletions to the bucket, destroying the off-volume copy too — iCloud was the last copy.

**PIN RESOLVED — nothing to remove (2026-07-25, post-v0.8.4).** The manual pin (`UPDATE blob_owners SET temp_until = NULL WHERE account_did = 'did:web:malpercio.dev'`) is **inert, not load-bearing**, and there is no removal step: it wrote the same NULL a legitimate reconcile pin writes, and once MM-473 fixed reconcile, each pass recomputes every row authoritatively — referenced blobs re-pinned on their own merits, owned-but-unreferenced rows **released straight through the pin** by reconcile's release loop (a pinned row is indistinguishable from "permanent", and releasing lapsed permanents is that loop's job). Live evidence: owned blob count went 540 at deploy → **532** (public `listBlobs` census) — 8 restore-surplus blobs (in the iCloud manifest but referenced by no record) were released and collected through the pin. The earlier "do NOT lift blind" reasoning was wrong for exactly this reason. All four MM-473 collections now 200 at limit=100 on prod; `getRepo` healthy.

**Incident close-out remaining:** verify the **mirror bucket** re-filled (~532 objects / `blob_mirror_synced_total` jump) — the incident deleted the bucket copies and the restore only refilled the local volume, so until confirmed, iCloud is still the only second copy. Plus one health glance: `blobGc.errors: 0` sustained, `blobUnownedCount: 0`, `uploadedBlobCount` ≈ `blobCount` on the account storage endpoint (MM-474 fields).

**Gotchas worth keeping:**
- "Visible in bsky" is NOT evidence the PDS holds a blob — `cdn.bsky.app` caches independently and renders long after the origin loses the bytes.
- Every operator-reachable blob read (`admin/accounts` `totalBytes`, `/v1/accounts/:id/storage`, `sync.listBlobs`, `repo.listMissingBlobs`, `sync.getBlob`) reads `blob_owners`. None distinguishes "ownership lost" from "bytes gone" — diagnosis needs a prod SQLite shell (MM-474).
- A `blob_gc` pass with `errors=N` still logs "pass complete" and refreshes its last-run timestamp, so the documented stale-timestamp alarm never fires. Grep WARN `reconcile failed` instead.
- `EZPDS_BLOBS_GC_INTERVAL_SECS=0` is rejected by config validation — not a way to disable GC.

Related: [[project_pds_hostname_migration]], [[project_wallet_icloud_backup_scope]].

**2026-07-25:** `did:web:malpercio.dev` lost **534 blobs** on Custos production (`custos-obsign`), recovered from the wallet's iCloud media backup (`restore_blob_backup`). Filed as MM-472 (urgent), MM-473, MM-474, MM-475.

**Cause chain.** NOT data loss — the repo is complete (`sync.getRepo` exports 3.3 MB successfully, and `build_car` reads every record block or errors, so a 200 proves all blocks present). The trigger is MM-473: **atrium-repo 0.1.8 `Node::entries_with_prefix` (mst.rs ~1070)** — a leaf key SHORTER than the prefix makes `key.get(..prefix.len())` return `None`, skipping the comparison and falling through to the unconditional push meant for Tree entries. Leak is governed by key length vs prefix length (NOT node topology; repro = long collection name + one short key like `zz.a/self`). Upstream main still broken as of 2026-07-25, 0.1.8 is latest — no version-bump fix. Sometimes one key leaks, sometimes hundreds (774 for one 5-record collection). Artifacts (frozen CAR + probe output) preserved in gitignored `linear-export/mm-473-artifacts/`. In `list_records_json`, `strip`'s `unwrap_or(key)` keeps the foreign key whole, the re-concatenated `<prefix><foreign-key>` resolves to nothing, and `blob_gc`'s `reconcile_account` throws `repo error: list records: record not found` on every pass. **That `unwrap_or` fallback is load-bearing**: passing the original key through would make `get_raw` succeed and serve foreign records under the wrong collection — fail-closed must be preserved by any fix. Reproducible live: `limit == record_count` → 200 (the bad entry is dropped by `entries.truncate(limit)`), `limit == count+1` → 500. 4 of 78 collections affected. Reconcile is the only thing that pins a blob permanent, and it errors on its first call (`collect_referenced_blob_cids`), so nothing was ever pinned. Phase 2's sweep is **global** and not gated on reconcile success, so 6h after upload (`blobs.temp_ttl_secs` default) it deleted all 534 ownership rows, physical rows, and files. `blob_mirror` then propagated the row deletions to the bucket, destroying the off-volume copy too — iCloud was the last copy.

**PIN RESOLVED — nothing to remove (2026-07-25, post-v0.8.4).** The manual pin (`UPDATE blob_owners SET temp_until = NULL WHERE account_did = 'did:web:malpercio.dev'`) is **inert, not load-bearing**, and there is no removal step: it wrote the same NULL a legitimate reconcile pin writes, and once MM-473 fixed reconcile, each pass recomputes every row authoritatively — referenced blobs re-pinned on their own merits, owned-but-unreferenced rows **released straight through the pin** by reconcile's release loop (a pinned row is indistinguishable from "permanent", and releasing lapsed permanents is that loop's job). (Measure carefully: health's `storage.blobCount` = server-wide PHYSICAL rows [540, incl. other accounts]; `listBlobs` = per-account OWNERSHIP rows [532 for this DID] — not comparable, an earlier "8 collected" inference conflated them.) The earlier "do NOT lift blind" reasoning was wrong because the release loop overrides the pin. All four MM-473 collections now 200 at limit=100 on prod; `getRepo` healthy; post-deploy health shows `blobGc {swept 0, errors 0}` fresh — reconcile genuinely green.

**Expected + benign:** the first post-v0.8.4 reconcile grace-clocked any restored-but-unreferenced blob (release + 6h), so a pass ~6.5h after the deploy boot may report `swept: N` / `blobCount` dropping below 540 — that's the restore surplus collecting correctly, not a regression.

**Incident close-out remaining:**
- **Mirror bucket refill unproven**: last-pass `blobMirror {swept: 0}` is consistent-with but not proof (per-pass snapshot; the OTel cumulative counter resets each boot). Confirm via yesterday's Railway logs (`blob mirror: uploaded` burst after the restore) or a direct bucket object count (≈540). Until then iCloud is the only second copy.
- **MM-474 fields are NOT on prod**: v0.8.4 predates PR #441 (health shows no `blobUnownedCount`). Merging → staging only; prod needs the next release. Run the unowned-blob / `uploadedBlobCount`≈`blobCount` checks after that release (or on staging).
- `blobScrub: null` since boot — fine (restored files were CID-verified at upload), but no file-integrity pass has run this process.

**Gotchas worth keeping:**
- "Visible in bsky" is NOT evidence the PDS holds a blob — `cdn.bsky.app` caches independently and renders long after the origin loses the bytes.
- Every operator-reachable blob read (`admin/accounts` `totalBytes`, `/v1/accounts/:id/storage`, `sync.listBlobs`, `repo.listMissingBlobs`, `sync.getBlob`) reads `blob_owners`. None distinguishes "ownership lost" from "bytes gone" — diagnosis needs a prod SQLite shell (MM-474).
- A `blob_gc` pass with `errors=N` still logs "pass complete" and refreshes its last-run timestamp, so the documented stale-timestamp alarm never fires. Grep WARN `reconcile failed` instead.
- `EZPDS_BLOBS_GC_INTERVAL_SECS=0` is rejected by config validation — not a way to disable GC.

Related: [[project_pds_hostname_migration]], [[project_wallet_icloud_backup_scope]].

---BODY---
Closes [MM-475](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-475/didweb-sovereign-sessions-and-wallet-confirmed-oauth-consent).

## Why

Both passwordless auth paths were hard-gated to `did:plc`, so a `did:web` account carrying no password had no way to authenticate at all — and every wallet-migrated account is passwordless, since the migration `createAccount` request has no `password` field and the server stores NULL by design.

That is more than a login inconvenience. `SessionProvider::full_access_client` is the seam every authenticated wallet operation on a Custos-hosted identity goes through, and its ladder ends at `NeedsUnlock` → biometric sovereign login. `restore_blob_backup` sits on that seam. So for a passwordless `did:web`, **the wallet's own iCloud media restore was reachable only while the refresh chain from migration survived** — once it lapsed, sovereign login 401'd on the `is_plc_did` gate and the recovery path was gone. This was on the critical path during the MM-472 recovery.

## The change is one lookup

Signature verification was already method-agnostic (`crypto::verify_did_key_signature` over a `did:key:` URI, P-256 and secp256k1). The only PLC-specific step was the authority lookup, and the `did:web` counterpart primitive already existed.

New `crates/pds/src/identity/authority.rs` exposes `authorized_signing_keys(state, did)`, dispatching `did:plc` → the existing `fetch_current_plc_state` path, `did:web` → `resolve_web_did_document` plus the policy below. ## Review: PR #442 (merged) — did:web sovereign sessions + wallet-confirmed OAuth consent (MM-475)

### Verdict

**Faithful to every decision we specified, and the security-critical properties all held up under inspection.** This is the right shape: one new module, two routes losing their duplicated gate, policy enforced server-side, UI deferral honest about why.

### Properties verified against the merged code

- **Ordering preserved on both routes.** Sovereign: syntax → freshness → *local-account gate* → signature → authority. Consent: pending-row binding → signature → authority. An unsigned or invalid probe still triggers no outbound fetch on either path.
- **Hosting gate fires before any network I/O**, and the route test proves it the strong way — the mock PLC mounts nothing and `plc.verify()` passes, plus the nonce is asserted unspent. Gate polarity correct (`enabled → refused`).
- **Predicate parity with `create_did.rs`** — `type`/`controller`/exact-id all enforced, each covered by a unit test, including the two cases I most wanted: `#atproto` is never authority, and duplicate `#device` entries fail closed rather than resolving by array order.
- **Opaque-rejection posture intact.** `Unauthorized` collapses into the routes' existing single messages; `Lookup` propagates with its own status — the same deliberate fail-closed-with-status posture the PLC path always had, now documented on the enum.
- **Cache untouchable.** Both arms resolve live, with the why-per-method comment (`rotationKeys` authority semantics; the cache is writable by `/v1/did-web/document`).
- **The malformed-DID fallthrough is safe**: `did:plc:tooshort` fails `is_plc_did`, doesn't match `did:web:`, lands in `unsupported_did_method` — it can never drift into the web arm.
- **Wallet**: 4 shapes → 2, deferral stated on-screen with a reason ("We would rather offer nothing than offer that" — exactly the honest-never-hype register), `didWebHosting` frozen to `'self'` with the un-deferral path documented in a comment, plumbing retained. ADR-0022 amendment records the policy, the gate's exactness, and the deferral, matching what we decided verbatim.

### Findings (follow-ups, nothing blocking)

1. **`crates/pds/AGENTS.md` is now stale** — the one gap. The routes table still describes `sovereign_session.rs` as "signed by a key in the hosted DID's authoritative current PLC `rotationKeys`," the `oauth_consent` module comment's counterpart in the table likewise, and the `identity/` module table doesn't list `authority.rs` at all. Nothing gates this (docs-check covers generated pages, not AGENTS.md), so it'll silently mislead the next session that loads it. Small PR or fold into the next dream-routine pass.
2. **Asymmetry worth one sentence somewhere**: the consent route (unlike sovereign, which has the local-account pre-gate) will run `web_authority` for a DID with no local account — the hosting probe finds no row, returns false, and the fetch proceeds. An attacker with a pending consent request and their own keypair can thus induce a fetch of `https://<their-domain>/.well-known/did.json`. Not a new class — `resolveDid` already offers arbitrary did:web resolution unauthenticated, the fetch is SSRF-hardened and rate-limited, and the pre-change PLC path had the same shape (fetch for any claimed DID) — but a local-account pre-check on the approve path would cost one indexed query and remove the asymmetry.
3. The acknowledged test gap (no route-level did:web happy path, since `did_web_document_url` hardcodes `https://`) is reasonable given the unit coverage — but it makes the **live verification the actual happy-path test**, which brings me to:

### The verification that closes this arc

Once this ships in the next release, `did:web:malpercio.dev` is the perfect live subject — your `did.json` already carries `#device`, and we confirmed `did_web_hosting_enabled_at` is NULL. The wallet's "Unlock identity" biometric flow against prod is the end-to-end proof. If it mints a session: MM-475 verified, and **the interim password can come off the account** — at which point every thread from this conversation (the OAuth lockout that started it, the blob incident it uncovered, and the recovery-path dependency that made this urgent) is actually, fully closed.
